scopeLimits: Analysis only; no gameplay edits, no CI dispatch, no universal level equivalence claim.
historyCheck: Fetched origin/main before selection. No open levels PR; only tooling/explained-negative-filters was open. Local main history checked for selection-line fixes.
hypothesis: JS selection growth cascades through newly selected points or loses diagonal neighbors compared with C.
supportedSetup: Boolean selection in a common map coordinate frame; Lua bigrm-2 and bigrm-5 wizard loads use their shipped programs. Seeds 28102026 and 28102027 were chosen before running; no seed search.
expectedC: Each existing point survives, and one-step neighbors selected by the eight direction-mask terms are added from the original selection. l_selection_grow clones first. W_RANDOM consumes one rn2(4).
observedJS: The clone is the output; all neighbor reads use this (the original selection). Each of the eight C predicates has the same offset and direction mask. The 512-neighborhood x 16-mask truth table, boundary clipping and random-direction checks pass. All four complete fresh streams match.
negativeProof: Both implementations compute oldSelection UNION masked-neighbors(oldSelection). C computes new neighbors in tmp then overlays; JS writes into clone while reading original. The eight terms correspond one-to-one, so no cascading growth occurs for Boolean selections in the same frame. Frame conversion, non-Boolean encoded values, and other APIs are outside this proof.
control: bigrm-2 seed 28102027 has percentage gate 84 (skip), against seed 28102026 gate 9 (take). bigrm-5 seed 28102026 gate 0 enters selection_filter_percent; seed 28102027 gate 94 skips. Full streams match in each pair.
rawClassificationCaveat: Adapter reports both bigrm-5 cases unresolved because the two-frame Lua trace names nhlib.percent, not the program. Raw status is preserved. Manual command-boundary inspection at step 25 sees the percent gates and (for seed 28102026) selection_filter_percent calls. This review does not upgrade the generic adapter or assert private-state equality.
prePublicationReview: Fetched main again; relevant C, level helpers, and discovery/recorder scripts are unchanged from measured base.
